subject: botany
question_text: Name the pigments responsible for the brown colour of Phaeophyceae and the red colour of Rhodophyceae.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack botany section, Chapter 4 Plant Kingdom, book p.7, VSAQ 3. Only one source book is held for botany — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand is physics-only and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card, not merely unrun. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Brown — fucoxanthin
lines: The brown colour of Phaeophyceae is due
steps.why: Brown algae also carry chlorophyll a and c, but the large amount of fucoxanthin masks the green and gives the brown colour.
common_mistakes: Writing 'phycoerythrin' for brown algae — that is the red-algae pigment.
Naming chlorophyll c as the colour cause — chlorophyll is green; fucoxanthin gives the brown.
steps.memory_tip: Fucus is a brown alga and fucoxanthin is the brown pigment — the pigment carries the alga's name.
steps.margin_note: One sentence naming the pigment earns the mark.

steps.label: Red — r-phycoerythrin
steps.why: Red algae owe their colour to the dominant pigment r-phycoerythrin, which masks their chlorophyll a and d. The book writes 'phycoerythrin'; NCERT's full name is r-phycoerythrin, and either is accepted.
common_mistakes: Swapping the two pigments between the groups.
Writing 'phycocyanin' — that pigment is blue; phycoerythrin is the red one.
steps.memory_tip: Erythrocytes are red blood cells — 'erythr' means red, so phycoerythrin is the red pigment.
steps.margin_note: Write each pigment beside its algal group, not as a bare list.

insider_note: Write the pigment and its group in the same sentence; a bare pigment name without its group can lose the mark.
